title: Fees and waiting
hook: You send coins and your wallet says "Pending". Ten minutes later, it still says pending. Did something go wrong?
card1: Every [[transaction]] pays a [[fee]] to the computers that add it to a [[block]]. The fee goes to the network, not to the person you are paying.
analogy1: A busy blockchain is like a bus with limited seats. When lots of people want to ride, those who offer more get on first. Low fees can wait for the next bus.
card2: Each new block added after the one with your transaction is a [[confirmation]]. The more confirmations, the harder it is to change. Shops often wait for a few before they count a payment as done.
card3: Fees change with how busy the network is. Before you send, look at the fee your wallet shows. Some networks are cheap, others can be expensive.

busy.prompt: You want to send 5 practice coins to a friend, but the network is very busy. Your wallet offers three fee levels.

lowest.label: Pick the lowest possible fee
lowest.before: You will pay the smallest fee and wait.
lowest.what: Your transaction waited for hours before it went through. Your friend had to wait too.
lowest.why: A low fee puts you at the back of the queue when the network is busy.
lowest.how: The computers that build blocks usually pick the transactions that pay the most.
lowest.realLife: If it isn't urgent, a low fee is fine. If it is, pay the normal fee.

normal.label: Pick the normal (recommended) fee
normal.before: You will pay the fee your wallet suggests.
normal.what: Your transaction was confirmed within minutes, and you paid a fair fee.
normal.why: Wallets suggest a fee based on how busy the network is right now.
normal.how: Your transaction got into one of the next blocks because its fee was in line with the others.
normal.realLife: The recommended fee is usually the right choice.

again.label: It's stuck, so send it again with a higher fee
again.before: You will send another 5 coins while the first one is still pending.
again.what: Both transactions went through in the end. Your friend got 10 coins instead of 5, and you paid two fees.
again.why: A pending transaction usually isn't lost. Sending again can mean paying twice.
again.how: Some wallets can properly speed up or cancel a pending transaction. Sending a new one is not the same thing.
again.realLife: If something is pending, wait and check it on a block explorer before doing anything else.

q1.a: The person you send coins to
q1.b: The network that processes the transaction
q1.explanation: Network fees go to the computers that add blocks. Some apps add their own fee on top, and they should show it to you.

q2.prompt: Your transaction has been pending for a long time. What is the best first step?
q2.b: Wait and check it on a block explorer
q2.c: Assume it's lost and ask your friend to send it back
q2.explanation: Pending usually just means waiting in the queue. Check before you do anything that could make you pay twice.

q3.a: A new block added after the one with your transaction
q3.b: An email from your wallet app
q3.c: Your friend saying they got the coins
q3.explanation: Each new block on top makes your transaction harder to change. That's why shops wait for confirmations.

misc.feeToReceiver: "The fee goes to the person I pay." It goes to the network that processes the transaction.
misc.feeToApp: "The wallet app keeps the fee." Network fees go to the computers that add blocks. If an app adds its own fee, it should show it.
misc.sendAgain: "Just send it again." The first one is probably still coming. You could pay twice.
misc.pendingLost: "Pending means lost." Usually it's just waiting in the queue.
misc.confirmEmail: "A confirmation is an email." It's a new block on the chain.
misc.confirmFriend: "My friend confirms it." Only the network confirms a transaction.

t1: Every [[transaction]] pays a [[fee]] to the network.
t2: When the network is busy, you pay more or wait longer.
t3: Pending isn't lost. Check before you send again.
talk1: Where else do people pay extra to go faster, like express delivery?
talk2: Would you rather pay more or wait longer? When does it matter?
